look_here_first: Start with one mature intact spikelet: the LOWER glume is usually about half the length of the UPPER glume (roughly 6–8 mm versus 11–15 mm, awns excluded) and normally has ONE vein. Then check the rooted plant for a persistent perennial tuft with many basal rolled leaves and hairs around the collar. Three awns and purple color confirm neither species by themselves.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora; Williamson — detailed county treatment of A. purpurea var. purpurea; Travis — USDA ARS herbarium collections from Austin/Travis County.

best_field_traits: On intact mature spikelets: lower glume roughly 6–8 mm, upper glume roughly 11–15 mm; typically 1 lower-glume vein (Kew GrassBase broad species treatment).
Perennial bunchgrass with persistent dense basal crown, usually many basal rolled/involute blades.
Collar hairs can be conspicuous in Texas material; recognize varieties and local variation.
A. oligantha: annual, often more openly branched, paired glumes subequal around 18–25 mm, and lower glume with 3–7 veins.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use glume relative length and LOWER glume vein count on a mature intact spikelet: A. purpurea has ~6–8 mm lower and ~11–15 mm upper (1-veined lower), while A. oligantha has ~18–25 mm subequal glumes (3–7-veined lower). Confirm a perennial vs annual basal crown; panicle shape and awn color are supporting only.
